Acard Privacy Policy

This is an English translation for convenience. If it differs from the Korean original, the Korean version (한국어 원문) prevails.

Effective date: October 24, 2026 · This policy may be revised after expert review during the beta; we will announce any change as described in section 12.

Acard ("Acard", "we") publishes this policy under Article 30 of the Korean Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) to explain how we process and protect your personal information and to handle related complaints quickly. It covers the Acard local app (the desktop app and the open-source open-notion-acard), the public site notes.example.com, the waitlist and the web app (Acard Cloud).

The short version

  • Your notes and files in the local app stay on your PC. We do not receive them and cannot see them.
  • The only thing the local app sends out by default is one update check. No usage statistics, crash reports or telemetry.
  • The personal information we receive is mainly the email address you give when joining the waitlist.
  • The web app (Acard Cloud) is currently for internal testing only and does not accept outside sign-ups.

1. Information we process, purposes, legal basis and retention

We process only the minimum needed for the purposes below. If a purpose changes we take the steps PIPA Article 18 requires, such as asking for consent again. We do not process sensitive information, unique identification numbers or pseudonymized information.

(1) Processed with your consent

PurposeItemsRetention
Waitlist sign-up, your place in line, invitations and launch news[Required] email
[Optional] AI tools you use, what you want to use Acard for, Discord username, how you found us (the source tag of the link)		Until you cancel. If you do not, deleted one year after the official launch
Record of the required consentsEmail, the items agreed to, the document version (effective date), time of consentOne year after the waitlist entry or account is deleted (to prove consent)
Account sign-up (web app, currently internal testing only)Email, password (stored only as a hash), name, email and profile picture provided by Google when you sign in with Google, sign-in records, notes and files you create, public handle, AI feature usage recordsUntil you delete the account

You may refuse consent. Without the required items you cannot join the waitlist or sign up. Leaving the optional questions unanswered has no effect on your sign-up.

(2) Processed without consent

2. What the local app sends and receives

Checked against the local app code as of October 24, 2026.

WhenWhatWhereHow to turn it off
When the installed desktop app startsAn update check. The request carries your IP address, app version and OS. New versions are downloaded from GitHub.notes.example.com/releases (Cloudflare); installers from github.comStart the app with the environment variable ACARD_NO_UPDATE=1. There is no in-app switch yet.
Only when you enter a license codeThe license code, an account identifier and a random device number created on this PCnotes.example.com/api/license/activateNothing is sent if you do not register.
Only when you connect an notes.example.com account and turn on backup, sync or publishingThe connected account, and the pages, backup files and attachments you chose to uploadnotes.example.comNothing is sent once you disconnect or turn the feature off.

The local app keeps your notes, files and settings in a data folder on your PC (for the desktop app on Windows, %APPDATA%\Acard). The local app has no AI feature that goes through Acard's servers. If you connect your own AI tool (for example Claude Code or Codex) to the local app, what you exchange with that tool is between you and its provider and never reaches Acard.

3. Children under 14

Children under 14 cannot join the waitlist or create an account, and we do not collect their personal information. We ask you to confirm you are 14 or older when you sign up, and if we learn we have information from a child under 14 we delete it right away.

4. Destruction

  • When the retention period ends or the purpose is achieved, we destroy the information without delay. If another law ever requires us to keep something, we will list the basis and items here and keep it separately. There is no such information now.
  • Electronic files are deleted from the database so they cannot be restored. We do not handle personal information on paper.
  • When you ask us to cancel your waitlist entry or delete your data, we do so within 7 days.

5. Provision to third parties

We do not provide your personal information to third parties, except where a law specifically requires it or an investigative authority requests it through legal procedure, and then only to that extent. We never use it for advertising or sell it.

  • Basis: for the waitlist and sign-up we ask for separate consent to the transfer on the sign-up form (Art. 28-8(1)1). For site access and mail forwarding, the transfer is processing and storage needed to provide the service you asked for and is disclosed in this policy (Art. 28-8(1)3(a)).
  • How to refuse and what happens: leave the transfer box unticked on the form, or withdraw a given consent by writing to hello@notes.example.com. Waitlist entries and accounts cannot be kept without this transfer, so refusing or withdrawing cancels the entry or account and we delete it. Web app AI features send nothing to Cloudflare AI unless you run them. Site access information is required to reach the site, so the only way to refuse it is to stop using the site.

8. Security measures

These are the measures we actually take today.

  • All traffic between your browser and our servers is encrypted with HTTPS. Stored data is encrypted with AES-256 by Supabase and Cloudflare.
  • Passwords are stored only as hashes.
  • Row-level security (RLS) is on for every table in the database, and waitlist entries and consent records can be read and written only with the service key held by the server. The key exposed to browsers cannot read or write these tables. The service key stays on the server.
  • Access to personal information is limited to the operator, and the admin screens work only for signed-in admin accounts.
  • Bursts of too many requests are blocked to limit unauthorized access and abuse.

9. Cookies and browser storage

  • The site uses only cookies for staying signed in (acard_at, acard_rt), handling Google sign-in (acard_pkce, acard_next, acard_gauth, kept for 10 minutes) and the display language (acard_lang, one year), plus browser storage that helps pages draw faster.
  • We use no advertising, analytics or tracking cookies and no third-party analytics tools.
  • You can block cookies in your browser settings (for example Chrome Settings > Privacy and security > Third-party cookies / Delete browsing data). Features that need sign-in will not work if you do.

10. Your rights and how to use them

  • You may ask to see, correct or delete your personal information, ask us to stop processing it, and withdraw consent. A legal representative or someone you authorize may ask on your behalf.
  • How: write to hello@notes.example.com from the email you used. After confirming the request came from that address we reply with the result within 10 days. If a legal reason prevents us from doing what you ask, we tell you why.
  • To cancel your waitlist entry or delete your account, ask the same way; we delete it within 7 days. Deleting an account removes the account, web app notes and files, and its waitlist, feedback and AI usage records. Local app data is on your PC, so you delete it yourself.

12. Changes and history

  • This policy applies from October 24, 2026.
  • We announce changes on the site 7 days before they take effect. Changes that are unfavorable to you, such as new items or purposes, are announced 30 days ahead with a before-and-after comparison.
